headline: CMS finalizes FY 2027 hospice payment update and spending-variation index
detail: CMS issued the FY 2027 hospice final rule with a 2.3% payment update and an aggregate cap of $36,174.75. The rule highlights Medicare non-hospice spending under a hospice election using the hospice service and spending variation index, a nine-measure claims-based scoring system, which CMS ties to concerns over fraud, waste and abuse in hospice care.

sector: HME/DME; Home Care; Pharmacy; Specialty Diagnostic Testing; Behavioral Health; Managed Long-Term Care
headline: New York imposes six-month Medicaid provider enrollment moratorium on high-risk categories
detail: New York's Medicaid Director announced an immediate moratorium of at least six months on new Medicaid provider enrollments, including affected change-of-ownership applications, for pharmacies, laboratories, DMEPOS suppliers, applied behavior analysis providers, licensed home care service agencies and managed long-term care plans. Reporting indicates all pending applications are discontinued regardless of review stage. The action responds to an April 23, 2026 CMS directive requiring states to revalidate every enrolled Medicaid provider within 24 months.
sourceAgency: NY State Dept. of Health (via Ropes & Gray)
sourceVerification: Secondary — verify against NY DOH primary notice
effectiveDate: Immediate, minimum six months from July 30, 2026

headline: HHS temporarily suspends federal funding for New York's Medicaid Fraud Control Unit
detail: Reporting indicates HHS announced in July 2026 a temporary suspension of federal funding for New York's Medicaid Fraud Control Unit, citing concerns regarding enforcement performance and program integrity. The action coincides with New York's provider enrollment moratorium and broader federal scrutiny of state Medicaid program integrity.
sourceVerification: Secondary — verify against HHS primary release
effectiveDate: Suspension period not specified in reporting

headline: CMS finalizes FY 2027 SNF payment update at 2.4%
detail: CMS finalized a 2.4% SNF PPS rate update (3.3% market basket less 0.9% productivity), an estimated $882.74 million aggregate increase. The rule also finalizes SNF QRP changes including an accelerated data submission timeline and a requirement to submit MDS assessments for all covered skilled residents regardless of payer. SNF VBP adjustments are estimated at a $203.60 million reduction in FY 2027.

headline: Adult-day-care owner pleads guilty to psychotherapy billing fraud
detail: DOJ announced a guilty plea involving more than $539,000 of allegedly false Medicare psychotherapy claims, including billing during hospitalizations, using former social workers' names and billing after beneficiaries had died.

sector: Skilled Nursing; Assisted Living; Home Health; Hospice; HME/DME
headline: Brewer and Crosswhite West fires remain active with Level 1–3 evacuations
detail: The July 25 official update reported active firefighting on the Brewer and Crosswhite West fires, continued extreme fire behavior and Red Flag conditions, Level 1, 2 and 3 evacuations, smoke impacts and threats to structures.

sector: HME/DME; Personal Care; Consumer Directed Services
headline: Missouri announces statewide DME and personal-care enrollment moratoria
detail: Effective August 1, 2026, Missouri will impose six-month statewide moratoria on new Medicaid enrollment applications for DMEPOS/DME and Consumer Directed Services/personal-care providers. Existing enrolled providers, revalidating providers and applications received before August 1 are not affected.
effectiveDate: Effective August 1, 2026 for six months; extensions permitted in six-month increments up to one year

headline: Minnesota requires prior authorization for all recuperative-care services
detail: Minnesota DHS made the Recuperative Care Service Prior Authorization form available July 24 and will require prior authorization for all recuperative-care services beginning August 1, 2026.

sector: Hospice; Behavioral Health; Specialty Diagnostic Testing; HME/DME; HCBS; Skilled Nursing
headline: Arizona proposes FFY 2027 Medicaid fee-for-service rate changes
detail: AHCCCS proposes FFS changes effective October 1, 2026, with an estimated aggregate payment increase of approximately $6.34 million. Hospice per diems and selected behavioral and diagnostic codes would change; DME and clinical laboratory schedules are budget neutral in aggregate, while HCBS and nursing-facility per diem rates remain unchanged.
sourceAgency: Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System
effectiveDate: Comments due August 24, 2026; proposed effective date October 1, 2026

sector: HCBS; Behavioral Health; Housing and Recovery Services
headline: Four men plead guilty to approximately $2.2 million Minnesota Medicaid fraud
detail: DOJ announced guilty pleas involving Minnesota's now-defunct Housing Stabilization Services program. The defendants allegedly billed for services not provided or inflated and used artificial intelligence to fabricate supporting records when questioned.

headline: Addiction-treatment operators sentenced in $4.8 million billing scheme
detail: DOJ announced prison sentences for three individuals involved in billing Medicare and Kentucky Medicaid more than $4.8 million through addiction-treatment facilities for services not provided or billed at higher complexity; restitution totaled $812,881.09.

headline: HHS removes disparate-impact liability from its Title VI regulations
detail: HHS OCR finalized amendments to 45 CFR Part 80 that remove regulatory provisions imposing or illustrating disparate-impact liability. The rule states that HHS will enforce Title VI against intentional discrimination and is effective July 24, 2026.

sector: Specialty Diagnostic Testing; Senior Living Referral Sources
headline: Dallas laboratory, owners and investors agree to pay $24 million
detail: DOJ announced that Magnolia Diagnostics and its owners agreed to pay $19.2 million over allegations of medically unnecessary respiratory pathogen panels billed for seniors receiving COVID-19 testing; investors agreed to pay an additional $4.8 million.

sector: Skilled Nursing; Assisted Living; Home Health; Hospice; HME/DME
headline: FEMA issues declaration for Oregon Akawa Butte Fire
detail: FEMA lists the Akawa Butte Fire as FM-5647-OR with an incident and declaration date of July 23, 2026. Official fire updates through July 26 reported evacuation orders, closures, smoke and continued hot, dry and windy conditions.

sector: All Medicaid-Exposed Services; Skilled Nursing; Hospitals
headline: CMS proposes provider-tax rule estimated to cut federal Medicaid spending by $246 billion
detail: CMS published a proposed rule implementing Section 71115 of H.R. 1, revising the regulatory framework for Medicaid provider taxes. CMS actuaries estimate the proposal would reduce federal Medicaid spending by approximately $246 billion over 10 years. Comments are due September 21, 2026. This is one of three major regulations implementing the reconciliation law's Medicaid financing and program integrity provisions.
sourceVerification: Secondary — verify against Federal Register primary text

headline: Medical-supply owner convicted in scheme attempting more than $30 million of billing
detail: DOJ announced a conviction involving purchased patient information, practitioner signatures and orders for orthotic braces and glucose monitors that beneficiaries did not want or need. The scheme attempted more than $30 million of federal billing and obtained more than $8 million.
effectiveDate: Conviction announced July 22, 2026; sentencing date not stated in release

sector: Behavioral Health; HCBS; HME/DME; Other Minnesota Medicaid Providers
headline: CMS defers $199 million of Minnesota federal Medicaid matching payments
detail: HHS stated that the Minnesota deferral involves claims across 14 service areas identified as higher risk while the state provides supporting documentation.

sector: Home Care; HCBS; Other Medi-Cal Providers
headline: California says an additional $646.4 million IHSS deferral brings deferred IHSS funds to $1.7 billion
detail: California DHCS stated on July 23 that CMS deferred an additional $646.4 million from in-home care and that, together with a prior May deferral, total deferred IHSS funds reached $1.7 billion. The state response does not change the federal characterization of deferrals as reviewable rather than permanent cuts.
sourceAgency: California Department of Health Care Services
effectiveDate: Federal documentation review ongoing; no fixed determination date announced

headline: Michigan budgets $184.3 million to mitigate federal eligibility changes
detail: Michigan's FY 2027 budget includes $184.3 million for federal requirement implementation, including $40 million for administration, $20 million for health navigators and $28 million for agencies handling Medicaid/SNAP work-requirement referrals.

headline: Fugitive arrested in alleged $547 million Medicare genetic-testing scheme
detail: DOJ announced the arrest of a defendant charged in an alleged nationwide scheme involving medically unnecessary genetic tests, deceptive marketing and kickbacks. The laboratories allegedly billed Medicare more than $547 million.
effectiveDate: Criminal case ongoing; no trial date stated in release

sector: All Medicaid-Exposed Services; Home Care; Behavioral Health; HME/DME
headline: HHS defers more than $1 billion of federal Medicaid payments to California and Minnesota
detail: HHS and CMS deferred $867.5 million for California and $199 million for Minnesota while the states provide documentation supporting claims. HHS described the actions as payment deferrals rather than permanent funding cuts.
effectiveDate: Documentation review underway; no final disallowance announced

headline: NeoGenomics agrees to pay $9.8 million over alleged referral compensation arrangements
detail: DOJ announced a $9.813 million settlement involving allegations of below-fair-market-value consulting services and variable referral-based compensation connected to laboratory test referrals.

headline: Federal emergency declaration for Texas flooding
detail: FEMA lists Texas Flooding EM-3649-TX with an incident period beginning July 12, 2026 and continuing; the emergency declaration was issued July 18.

headline: OIG identifies Colorado EVV weaknesses and Medicaid personal-care overpayments
detail: OIG found Colorado did not verify all personal-care visits through its electronic visit verification system and recommended refunding an estimated $8.0 million federal share while resolving an additional $45.7 million set aside for allowability review.

headline: FEMA declaration for Washington Kaiser Canyon Fire
detail: FEMA lists the Kaiser Canyon Fire as FM-5646-WA, with an incident period beginning July 16, 2026 and continuing.

sector: Skilled Nursing; Assisted Living; Home Health; Hospice; HME/DME
headline: FEMA declares fire disaster in OR: Lower Dry Creek Fire
detail: FEMA declaration FM-5645-OR for OR. Incident type: Fire. Incident period began 2026-07-15. Declared 2026-07-16. Facility-level operational impact requires review.

headline: OIG finds inconsistent state oversight of Medicaid MCO provider-fraud referrals
detail: OIG found state contract requirements and referral timeframes varied widely, including referral periods from one to 270 days and some contracts without a specific timeframe or clear enforcement provisions.

headline: CMS launches national risk-based nursing-home survey approach
detail: CMS announced a national risk-based survey approach built from a pilot across 22 states. All nursing homes remain subject to survey at least every 15 months, and implementation begins in September 2026.

headline: Senior housing occupancy reaches 89.9%, twentieth consecutive quarterly increase
detail: NIC MAP reported national senior housing occupancy of 89.9% in Q2 2026, up 0.4 points from 89.5% in Q1 and marking the twentieth consecutive quarterly increase. Occupancy met or exceeded 90% in 15 of 31 primary markets. Boston (93.3%), San Francisco (92.7%) and Baltimore (91.8%) led; Miami (86.2%) and Atlanta (86.5%) lagged. Occupied units rose to 639,650. Year-over-year inventory growth was 0.4%, with fewer than 16,000 units under construction.

sector: Skilled Nursing; Behavioral Health; Podiatry; Wound Care
headline: OIG estimates $19.5 million of improper Medicare Part B services for nursing-home residents
detail: OIG estimated that Novitas improperly paid about $19.5 million for selected evaluation and management, psychotherapy and podiatry services provided to nursing-home residents that did not meet Medicare requirements.

headline: Labcorp agrees to pay $14.5 million over alleged unnecessary urine drug testing
detail: DOJ announced a $14.5 million False Claims Act settlement involving allegations that Labcorp billed Medicare for medically unnecessary urine drug testing under its ToxAssure Comprehensive panel.

headline: Clinical laboratory fee reductions can phase up to 15% annually
detail: CMS states CLFS data reporting runs May 1-July 31, 2026 for Jan-Jun 2025 data; beginning CY 2027, statutory payment reductions can phase up to 15% per year through CY 2029.
effectiveDate: Reporting deadline July 31, 2026; cuts begin CY 2027

headline: CMS proposes expanded valuation for timed behavioral health services
detail: CMS proposes including tobacco-cessation and SBIRT services in the final year of the upward RVU transition for timed behavioral-health codes.

headline: CY 2027 Medicare physician conversion factors proposed to decline
detail: CMS proposes a $33.17 qualifying-APM conversion factor (-1.19%) and $32.84 non-qualifying factor (-1.68%), partly because the one-year 2.5% CY 2026 increase expires.

sector: Behavioral Health; Adult Day; HCBS; Home Care; Recuperative Care
headline: Minnesota high-risk Medicaid provider enrollment moratorium enters extended period
detail: CMS approved Minnesota's extension of its temporary enrollment moratorium for providers of 12 of 14 designated high-risk services. From July 27, 2026 through January 27, 2027, DHS will not accept new applications or process pending enrollment submissions for the covered services; the EIDBI moratorium is separately extended through October 31, 2026.
effectiveDate: Effective July 27, 2026 through January 27, 2027; EIDBI through October 31, 2026

sector: Hospitals; Home Health; HME/DME; Medicaid Providers
headline: Typhoon Bavi triggers HHS PHE and CMS waivers
detail: HHS declared a PHE following Typhoon Bavi. CMS made blanket waivers and flexibilities available retroactive to July 2 and permitted replacement of damaged DMEPOS items.
effectiveDate: PHE active; flexibilities retroactive to July 2

headline: North Carolina fully funds Medicaid for the year
detail: North Carolina's first full budget in more than two years fully funds Medicaid for the year.

sector: Behavioral Health; Developmental Disability; HCBS; Residential Services
headline: Virginia authorizes 2% Medicaid increases for selected developmental-disability waiver services
detail: Virginia's enacted budget authorizes a 2% rate increase effective July 1, 2026 for specified day, employment, group-home, sponsored-residential, supported-living and related waiver services.

sector: Home Health; Hospice; HME/DME; Other Medicare Providers
headline: CMS proposes broader retroactive revocation and ownership-related enrollment actions
detail: The CY 2027 home-health rule proposes additional grounds for retroactive Medicare enrollment revocation, new denial or revocation authority tied to owners and managing personnel, and enforcement of reenrollment requirements after specified majority-ownership changes.

headline: CMS proposes DME documentation relief plus new sourcing data
detail: CMS proposes that an identical replacement item would not require a repeat face-to-face exam when original documentation exists; it also proposes a country-of-origin field in competitive-bidding submissions.

headline: CY 2027 home health payments proposed to rise 2.4% in aggregate
detail: CMS estimates aggregate HHA payments would increase 2.4% ($420 million), including a 2.1% payment update and a -3.0% temporary adjustment to the CY 2027 base payment rate.

sector: Skilled Nursing; Assisted Living; Home Health; Hospice; HME/DME
headline: FEMA declares flood disaster in MI: Severe Storms, Tornadoes, And Flooding
detail: FEMA declaration DR-4925-MI for MI. Incident type: Flood. Incident period began 2026-04-10. Declared 2026-06-30. Facility-level operational impact requires review.

headline: Washington SPA would increase swing-bed rates and continue nursing-facility PDPM add-on
detail: Washington SPA 26-0017 would increase the swing-bed daily rate, continue the Patient Driven Payment Model transition add-on and implement a daily add-on for increased Medicaid bed-license fees.
effectiveDate: Effective July 1, 2026; comments due July 31, 2026; CMS approval pending

sector: Assisted Living; Adult Family Homes; Home Care; HCBS
headline: Washington proposes Medicaid rate increases for assisted living and HCBS providers
detail: Washington SPA 26-0016 increases assisted-living, adult-family-home, individual-provider and agency-provider Medicaid rates; the notice includes a 10% increase in the weighted adult-day-health daily rate to $123.06.
effectiveDate: Effective July 1, 2026; public comment period through July 31, 2026

headline: Florida increases community and home-care funding for seniors
detail: The budget adds $7.5 million, bringing total funding to $131 million, for Community Care for the Elderly and Home Care for the Elderly programs.
sourceAgency: Florida Executive Office of the Governor

sector: Skilled Nursing; Long-Term Care; Disability Services
headline: Florida funds $214.6 million of targeted provider-rate increases
detail: Florida's FY 2026-27 budget includes $214.6 million for targeted rate increases across healthcare, long-term care and disability-service programs.
sourceAgency: Florida Executive Office of the Governor

headline: DOJ alleges $89 million diagnostic cardiovascular testing scheme
detail: The national takedown includes an alleged $89 million scheme involving diagnostic cardiovascular testing.

headline: DOJ identifies another $3.7 billion of alleged DME catheter fraud
detail: The takedown describes additional alleged false claims tied to DME and urinary catheters totaling about $3.7 billion.

headline: Large behavioral-health fraud allegations span multiple states
detail: DOJ cited alleged behavioral-health schemes of $49 million in Virginia, $44 million in Arizona and $67 million in Illinois Medicaid billing.

headline: DOJ describes alleged $27.7 million hospice fraud scheme
detail: The national takedown includes allegations that a hospice owner and marketers enrolled non-terminal patients and purchased deceased-person information in a $27.7 million scheme.

headline: National takedown charges 455 defendants in alleged $6.5 billion fraud
detail: DOJ announced 455 defendants charged in connection with more than $6.5 billion in alleged healthcare fraud.

headline: OIG estimates $255.1 million of potential Medicare hospice savings from eligibility reviews
detail: OIG found that 45 of 100 sampled initial certification periods lacked support for terminal eligibility or required documentation and estimated $255.1 million of potential savings if MACs performed targeted reviews of certain new hospice enrollees.

headline: OIG identifies unsupported nursing-home staffing hours in Payroll-Based Journal data
detail: OIG estimated that about 938,000 registered-nurse hours, or 5% of the reviewed sampling frame, were unsupported in March 2024 PBJ data and recommended stronger CMS audit and education processes.

headline: OIG finds at least $13.9 million of excess California Medicaid laboratory reimbursement
detail: OIG found California paid more than permitted for millions of clinical diagnostic laboratory services, identified $13.9 million of excess reimbursement including a $7.6 million federal share, and identified a further $29.3 million of potential excess payments.

headline: OIG finds 95% of appealed Medicare Advantage SNF admission denials were overturned
detail: In OIG's review, 19 Medicare Advantage organizations denied 12% of SNF admission requests; only 18% of denials were appealed, but 95% of appealed denials were overturned.

sector: Skilled Nursing; Home Health; Hospice; HME/DME; Other Healthcare Services
headline: Hawaii severe-storm and flooding public health emergency renewed
detail: HHS renewed the Hawaii public health emergency effective June 8, 2026 for continuing consequences of severe storms, flooding, landslides and mudslides; CMS lists emergency waivers and flexibilities.
effectiveDate: PHE remains active subject to renewal or termination

headline: Medicaid community-engagement requirement set for 2027
detail: Certain adults must demonstrate 80 hours per month of qualifying work, education or community service. States generally must implement by January 1, 2027.

headline: New York budget adds over $950 million for nursing homes and ALPs
detail: The enacted FY 2027 budget includes more than $950 million in new and recurring support for nursing homes and Assisted Living Programs, within broader health-system funding.

headline: Ohio tightens Medicaid provider revalidation and fraud controls
detail: Ohio approved emergency provider-revalidation rules after announcing additional Medicaid fraud-prevention initiatives and seeking a temporary provider-enrollment moratorium.

headline: Nationwide Medicare enrollment moratorium for HHAs and hospices
detail: CMS imposed a six-month nationwide moratorium on initial HHA and hospice applications, including non-exempt changes in majority ownership; it may be extended in six-month increments.

headline: PACS Group Q1 2026: revenue $1.42B, net income $80.7M, investigations unresolved
detail: Q1 2026 revenue rose 11% year over year to $1.42 billion with net income of $80.7 million and diluted EPS of $0.50. Operating cash flow was $236.3 million. Adjusted EBITDA rose 75% to $170.4 million. The company reported 323 facilities and 35,516 beds, occupancy of 90.9%, roughly $800 million of available liquidity and net leverage of 0.1x. The filing discloses multiple ongoing DOJ investigations, an SEC enforcement investigation, securities class and derivative actions, self-insurance liabilities of $346.9 million, and material weaknesses in internal controls. The board authorized a $250 million share repurchase effective May 7, 2026.

sector: Senior Housing; Medical Office; Life Science
headline: Diversified Healthcare Trust Q1 2026: leverage improves to 7.8x, FFO guidance raised
detail: DHC reported Q1 2026 revenue of $366.5 million and a net loss of $43.3 million ($0.18 per share), narrowed year over year. Same-property SHOP NOI rose 13.5% to $44.3 million with margins of 14.9%; medical office and life science same-property cash NOI grew 3.0% with occupancy of 95.3%. Normalized FFO more than doubled to $33.1 million. Net debt to annualized Adjusted EBITDAre improved to 7.8x from 8.1x, with EBITDAre to interest expense at 2.0x. Liquidity was $271 million including $121 million cash and an undrawn $150 million secured revolver.

headline: State-level staffing mandates fill the gap left by federal rollback; New York imposing penalties
detail: With the federal staffing mandate repealed, state-level requirements have become the operative constraint. New York has begun imposing penalties on facilities failing to meet a minimum 3.5 hours of direct care per resident per day. Operators report being penalized during documented workforce shortages. State mandates now represent the primary staffing-cost exposure for multi-state operators.
sourceVerification: Trade press — not a primary source

headline: Federal Medicaid matching eligibility narrows for certain noncitizen groups
detail: Beginning October 1, 2026, federal financial participation is restricted to specified eligible groups, with exceptions that include Emergency Medicaid and certain coverage for lawfully residing children and pregnant women.

headline: CMS proposes stronger hospice utilization transparency and oversight
detail: The proposed rule introduces a nine-metric Service and Spending Variation Index and would require the hospice election addendum for all Medicare beneficiaries at election.

headline: FY 2027 hospice payment rate proposed to increase 2.4%
detail: CMS proposes a 2.4% hospice rate increase, estimated at $785 million, and a FY 2027 aggregate cap of $36,210.11. Noncompliant HQRP providers would receive a 1.6% reduction versus the prior year.

headline: FY 2027 SNF PPS proposed payment update
detail: CMS proposes a 2.4% SNF PPS rate update (3.2% market basket less 0.8% productivity). SNFs missing QRP reporting lose 2 percentage points; SNF VBP withholds 2% of Medicare FFS Part A payments.

headline: Washington supplemental budget backfills selected Medicaid and health programs
detail: The signed supplemental budget includes $15 million to backfill Medicaid funding for Planned Parenthood and $19.8 million for healthcare coverage for approximately 1,200 Washington residents.

headline: Quipt Home Medical completes take-private; delisted from NASDAQ and TSX
detail: Quipt completed the plan of arrangement on March 16, 2026 following a final order from the Supreme Court of British Columbia. Affiliates of Kingswood and Forager acquired all outstanding shares at US$3.65 per share; options and RSUs were cashed out and cancelled. Shares were delisted from NASDAQ and the TSX at close of business March 17, 2026, and the company intends to cease public reporting in both Canada and the United States. Trade coverage described the transaction as ending a contentious nine-month process.
sourceVerification: Trade press — corroborated by company release

headline: Health Affairs study finds state staffing mandates raised staffing with minimal closures
detail: A Health Affairs study published March 3, 2026 examining state nursing home minimum staffing mandates from 2010 to 2023 found increased staffing levels with minimal impact on facility finances or closures. Increases were driven mainly by LPNs and nursing assistants. Researchers noted unexplained increases in net revenue, with possible explanations including payer-mix shifts toward higher-margin Medicare patients, states raising Medicaid daily rates, or capital previously obscured through related-party transactions.

headline: Nationwide Medicare enrollment moratorium for DME medical-supply companies
detail: CMS imposed a six-month moratorium on initial applications and non-exempt majority-ownership changes for listed DMEPOS medical-supply company types.

headline: Hospice telehealth recertification extended through 2027 with restrictions
detail: CAA 2026 extends telehealth face-to-face recertification through December 31, 2027, but bars it in moratorium/enhanced-oversight situations and requires claim modifiers/codes beginning January 1, 2027.

headline: CMS finalizes restrictions on Medicaid provider-tax structures
detail: The rule prohibits higher tax rates on Medicaid business than non-Medicaid business and blocks indirect structures; transition periods extend through calendar 2026, state FY 2027 or state FY 2028 depending on tax type and approval timing.
effectiveDate: Transition deadlines vary through state FY 2028

headline: Medicaid cuts under reconciliation law identified as principal 2026 sector risk
detail: Trade coverage identifies OBBBA Medicaid reductions as the dominant risk for skilled nursing in 2026, as state Medicaid offices face new federal enrollment requirements alongside shrinking federal match. Operators in Pennsylvania, Virginia, North Carolina and Ohio were cited as facing state budget deficits after pandemic stimulus funding expired. Medicaid funds roughly 66% of nursing home revenue, and states facing tighter federal funding may freeze or reduce daily reimbursement rates.
sourceVerification: Trade press — not a primary source
effectiveDate: Cuts not expected to hit in full until Q4 2026

headline: SNF census recovery continues as staffing mandate rollback removes overhang
detail: Industry survey data shows 39.3% of skilled nursing providers have returned to pre-pandemic census, up from 38.0% a year earlier and 30.8% in 2024. Roughly two-thirds expect to reach strong census soon, and 89.25% expect occupancy to hold or increase in 2026. Staffing remained the top concern, cited by 79% of nurse leaders. The staffing mandate rollback removed a major cost threat, though Medicare Advantage expansion and payment reform continue to pressure margins.
sourceVerification: Trade press — not a primary source

sector: Senior Housing; Medical Office; Life Science
headline: Diversified Healthcare Trust repays 2026 notes, completes $605M of asset sales
detail: DHC repaid in full its zero coupon senior secured notes due 2026 on December 29, 2025 using cash on hand and asset sale proceeds, releasing 45 collateral properties representing roughly $850 million of gross book value. DHC completed the sale of 69 non-core properties for approximately $605 million during 2025, including 37 properties for $250 million in Q4. The company reported no debt maturities until 2028 and full availability under its revolving credit facility. All 116 SHOP communities managed by AlerisLife were transitioned to new operators as of December 31, 2025.

headline: Minnesota implements 3.19% increases for selected home-health and therapy services
detail: Minnesota DHS lists a 3.19% market-basket increase for home-health aide, skilled nursing, occupational therapy, physical therapy, respiratory therapy and speech therapy services.

headline: Quipt Home Medical agrees to be acquired by Kingswood and Forager at $3.65 per share
detail: Quipt entered an arrangement agreement dated December 14, 2025 with affiliates of Kingswood Capital Management and Forager Capital Management to acquire all outstanding shares for US$3.65 per share in cash, a 162% premium to the unaffected May 19, 2025 price. Quipt reported Q4 2025 revenue of $68.3 million, up 11% year over year, and fiscal 2025 revenue of $254.5 million, a slight decline.

headline: CMS interim final rule withdraws federal nursing home minimum staffing standards
detail: CMS published an interim final rule on December 3, 2025 withdrawing the 2024 minimum staffing standards for long-term care facilities, which had required 24/7 onsite RN coverage and 3.47 hours per resident day. The rule took effect February 2, 2026. Combined with the reconciliation law's moratorium on implementation through 2034 and court vacatur, the mandate is effectively neutralized. Analysis cited roughly $51.83 billion of net 10-year regulatory savings.
sourceVerification: Secondary — verify against Federal Register text

sector: Skilled Nursing; Behavioral Health; Other Medicaid Managed Care Providers
headline: Federal law limits certain Medicaid state-directed payment levels
detail: The law limits specified state-directed payments for hospital, nursing-facility and certain practitioner services to 100% of published Medicare rates in expansion states and 110% in non-expansion states, with grandfathering and phase-down provisions beginning in later rating periods.
effectiveDate: Grandfathering transitions toward rating periods beginning on or after January 1, 2028

headline: Federal law shortens Medicaid retroactive eligibility periods
detail: For applications made on or after January 1, 2027, retroactive eligibility is limited to one month for the Medicaid adult expansion group and two months for other Medicaid groups.

headline: Medicaid adult expansion renewals move from annual to every six months
detail: Beginning with renewals scheduled on or after January 1, 2027, affected Medicaid adult expansion beneficiaries must have eligibility redetermined every six months, with limited exceptions.

headline: PACS Group receives DOJ subpoena over Medicare billing and 1135 waiver practices
detail: Per company SEC filings, PACS received a DOJ HIPAA subpoena relating to an investigation into possible false statements to the government. Requests cover 1135 COVID waiver practices, Medicare Part B billing for respiratory and sensory integration therapy, change of insurance enrollment, cost waivers for co-pays and deductibles, and Medicare bad debt reimbursement. Separately, the SEC Division of Enforcement is investigating the company's accounting, financial reporting, disclosure, and internal controls.

headline: PACS Group loses 70% of market capitalization amid billing allegations and delayed filings
detail: Following the short-seller report, PACS faced allegations of deceptive Medicare billing, a federal regulatory investigation, delayed financial reporting, and a securities class action (Manchin v. PACS Group, S.D.N.Y.). The class period runs April 11, 2024 through November 5, 2024. Complaint alleges the reported turnaround was driven by improper acquisition of Medicare benefits and falsified patient records.
sourceVerification: Secondary — plaintiff firm release; verify against court docket

headline: Hindenburg Research alleges fraudulent Medicare billing at PACS Group
detail: A short-seller report based on a five-month investigation and interviews with former employees alleged fraudulent charting and billing practices, including a company-wide scheme tied to COVID-era 1135 waiver use. The report noted PACS generated 47.6% of 2022 revenue from Medicare versus 28.6% at The Ensign Group. Shares fell roughly 40% on publication. The report cited no active government investigations at the time.
sourceVerification: Trade press — not a primary source

headline: Prior-authorization API requirements approach 2027 implementation
detail: CMS prior-authorization and interoperability requirements include provisions already effective in 2026, with major API requirements primarily beginning January 1, 2027.
